title: MARLA: A Conceptual Scaffold for Regulatory Learning under the EU AI Act
abstract: arXiv:2609.04877v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The EU AI Act positions regulation as part of the infrastructure for safe, trustworthy and market-ready innovation. Realising this ambition requires regulatory learning: the evidence generated during implementation must be translated into governance and legal knowledge that supports consistent interpretation, effective oversight, and adaptation as technologies evolve. Yet the actors who produce this evidence and those who rely on it operate in different professional worlds. This paper proposes MARLA (Map, Assess, Report, Learn, Adapt), a conceptual scaffold organising regulatory learning as a five-stage cycle centred on the implementation of legal requirements into socio-technical practices, situated at the Local, National and European levels of the AI Act's governance architecture. Deliberately non-prescriptive, MARLA gives technical and legal stakeholders a shared vocabulary in which each of the first three stages generates its own doc

translated_title: MARLA：欧盟《人工智能法案》下监管学习的概念框架
translated_abstract: 欧盟《人工智能法案》将监管定位为安全、可信且面向市场创新的基础设施的一部分。实现这一愿景需要监管学习：在实施过程中产生的证据必须被转化为治理和法律知识，以支持一致的解释、有效的监督以及随技术演进的适应性调整。然而，产生这些证据的行为主体与依赖这些证据的行为主体分属不同的专业领域。本文提出了MARLA（绘制、评估、报告、学习、适应），这是一个概念性框架，将监管学习组织为一个五阶段循环，其核心是将法律要求落实为社会技术实践，并定位于《人工智能法案》治理架构的地方、国家和欧洲三个层面。MARLA刻意保持非规定性，为技术和法律领域的利益相关者提供了一个共享的词汇体系，其中前三个阶段各自产生自己的文件
tldr: 本文提出MARLA概念框架，将欧盟《人工智能法案》下的监管学习组织为“绘制-评估-报告-学习-适应”五阶段循环，为技术和法律利益相关者搭建跨领域协作的共享词汇体系。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes MARLA, a deliberately non-prescriptive conceptual scaffold that organizes regulatory learning under the EU AI Act as a five-stage Map-Assess-Report-Learn-Adapt cycle, providing technical and legal stakeholders with a shared vocabulary.
